namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference

/-!
# The holomorphic hull on a direct-sum-of-fields presentation (taxis #45)

Following IUT III, Remark 3.9.5, the **holomorphic hull** of a region `U` of a
tensor-packet — presented as a direct sum of fields with holomorphic integral structure
`O` (`Iut.DirectSumPresentation`) — is the smallest region of the form `a · O`
containing `U`, where every direct-summand component of `a` is nonzero
(`Iut.DirectSumPresentation.IsHullRegion`).

## Design and honesty boundary

Whether a least hull region containing `U` *exists* is a genuine theorem of
nonarchimedean/archimedean local-field theory (discreteness of the value group, and the
relative-compactness and finite-log-volume hypotheses of IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)); its
proof belongs to the local-field infrastructure tracked in taxis #4 and is **not**
assumed silently here. Instead:

* `IsLeastHullRegionIn 𝓗` states what it means for a region to be *the* hull of `U`
  relative to a class `𝓗` of hull regions (`IsLeastHullRegion` is the case of all hull
  regions `a · O`);
* `HullSystem` packages, as explicit structure fields, a class `Admissible` of regions
  and a class `HullRegions` of hull regions `a · O` containing the integral region,
  together with a hull operation and its defining least-hull-region properties relative
  to `HullRegions`, plus the explicit relative-compactness requirement on admissible
  regions. The class `HullRegions` is part of the data because the hull regions among
  which a least one exists depend on the place: at a nonarchimedean place they are all
  regions `a · O` with `a` a unit; at the archimedean place they are the real radial
  scalings `t · B_I` of the product of unit balls (IUT IV, Proposition 1.5(iii)), among
  arbitrary units a least region need not exist. Producing a `HullSystem` for the
  concrete packets is the certificate discharged by the local-field project (taxis #4);
  nothing in this repository asserts that such a system exists.

Given a `HullSystem`, the four defining elementary properties requested by taxis #45
are **proved** below, not postulated:

1. hull regions are fixed points (`HullSystem.hull_eq_self`);
2. extensivity `U ⊆ hull U` (`HullSystem.subset_hull`);
3. monotonicity (`HullSystem.hull_mono`);
4. the intersection characterization (`HullSystem.hull_eq_sInter`), over the class
   `HullRegions`.

Idempotency (`HullSystem.hull_idem`) follows, and the hull is exposed as a genuine
`ClosureOperator` on the class of admissible regions (`HullSystem.closureOperator`).

**Convention for non-relatively-compact regions.** Admissible regions are required to be
relatively compact (`HullSystem.relCompact_of_admissible`); the hull operation is a total
function on regions, but outside the admissible class its values carry no meaning and no
properties are recorded for them. This is the convention requested by taxis #45
("specify separately the convention for non-relatively-compact regions"): such regions
are simply outside the domain of the recorded interface, rather than being assigned an
ad-hoc improper hull.

## Source correspondence

* Definition of the hull as the least `a · O ⊇ U` with all components of `a` nonzero:
  IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i).
* Relative-compactness and finite-log-volume hypotheses: IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)–(ii).
  The finite-log-volume hypothesis is expressed at the point where a `HullSystem` is
  constructed from log-volume data, since the hull module deliberately does not depend
  on the log-volume module (taxis #44).
-/

namespace Iut

universe u v

namespace DirectSumPresentation

variable {C : Type u} {P : DirectSumPresentation.{u, v} C}

/-- `R` is *the* holomorphic hull of `U` relative to a class `𝓗` of hull regions: a
member of `𝓗` containing `U` and least among the members of `𝓗` containing `U`
(IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)). -/
def IsLeastHullRegionIn (P : DirectSumPresentation C) (𝓗 : Set (Set P.Total))
    (U R : Set P.Total) : Prop :=
  R ∈ 𝓗 ∧ U ⊆ R ∧ ∀ R' ∈ 𝓗, U ⊆ R' → R ⊆ R'

end DirectSumPresentation

open DirectSumPresentation

/-- A **hull system** on a direct-sum-of-fields presentation: a class of admissible
regions, required to be relatively compact, on which a holomorphic hull operation with
the defining property of IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i) is supplied.

This is the interface seam of taxis #45: existence of the least hull region is a
theorem of local-field theory (taxis #4) recorded here as explicit fields, never as
axioms. All four elementary properties of the hull are then *proved* from these fields
(`hull_eq_self`, `subset_hull`, `hull_mono`, `hull_eq_sInter`). -/
structure HullSystem {C : Type u} (P : DirectSumPresentation.{u, v} C) :
    Type (max u v) where
  /-- The class of admissible regions on which the hull operates. In the intended
  instantiation: nonempty relatively compact regions of finite nonzero log-volume with
  nonzero component projections (IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)). -/
  Admissible : Set (Set P.Total)
  /-- Explicit hypothesis: admissible regions are relatively compact. Regions that are
  not relatively compact are outside the domain of this interface. -/
  relCompact_of_admissible : ∀ U ∈ Admissible, IsCompact (closure U)
  /-- The class of hull regions among which the hull is least: at a nonarchimedean place
  all regions `a · O` with `a` a unit, at the archimedean place the real radial scalings
  `t · B_I` (IUT IV, Proposition 1.5(iii)). -/
  HullRegions : Set (Set P.Total)
  /-- Members of the class are hull regions `a · O` with all components of `a` units. -/
  isHullRegion_of_mem : ∀ R ∈ HullRegions, P.IsHullRegion R
  /-- The holomorphic integral region belongs to the class. -/
  integralRegion_mem : P.integralRegion ∈ HullRegions
  /-- The holomorphic hull operation. Values outside `Admissible` are junk. -/
  hull : Set P.Total → Set P.Total
  /-- The hull of an admissible region is the least member of `HullRegions` containing it
  (IUT III, Remark 3.9.5(i)). -/
  isLeastHullRegion_hull : ∀ U ∈ Admissible, P.IsLeastHullRegionIn HullRegions U (hull U)
  /-- The admissible class is stable under the hull operation, so that the hull is a
  closure operator on admissible regions. -/
  hull_admissible : ∀ U ∈ Admissible, hull U ∈ Admissible

namespace HullSystem

variable {C : Type u} {P : DirectSumPresentation.{u, v} C} (H : HullSystem P)

variable {U V : Set P.Total}

/-- **Extensivity** (taxis #45, property 2): `U` is contained in its holomorphic hull. -/
lemma subset_hull (hU : U ∈ H.Admissible) : U ⊆ H.hull U :=
  (H.isLeastHullRegion_hull U hU).2.1

/-- Minimality: the hull of `U` is contained in every member of the class of hull
regions containing `U`. -/
lemma hull_le (hU : U ∈ H.Admissible) {R : Set P.Total}
    (hR : R ∈ H.HullRegions) (hUR : U ⊆ R) : H.hull U ⊆ R :=
  (H.isLeastHullRegion_hull U hU).2.2 R hR hUR

/-- **Hull regions are fixed points** (taxis #45, property 1): if an admissible region
is itself a member of the class of hull regions, it is its own hull. -/
theorem hull_eq_self (hU : U ∈ H.Admissible) (h : U ∈ H.HullRegions) : H.hull U = U :=
  Set.Subset.antisymm (H.hull_le hU h subset_rfl) (H.subset_hull hU)

end HullSystem

end Iut

end AbcAdaptation.Reference
payload.natural_language_statement:
**Formal-code readback**

**English**

Let u and v be universe levels, let C : Type u be any type, and let P : DirectSumPresentation.{u,v} C. For each c : C, P specifies a commutative ring A_c : Type v, an arbitrary topology on A_c and a subset I_c ⊆ A_c. Write T = ∏c A_c for P.Total, equipped with the product topology, and J = {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ I_c} for P.integralRegion. For a ∈ T, P.scaledIntegral a is {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • I_c}, where a(c) • I_c = {a(c)y | y ∈ I_c}. P.IsHullRegion R means that there is a single a ∈ T such that every a(c) is a unit in A_c and R = P.scaledIntegral a. The index type C need not be finite, the subsets I_c need not be subrings, and continuity of multiplication is not assumed.

For any family 𝓗 ⊆ Set T and subsets U,R ⊆ T, P.IsLeastHullRegionIn 𝓗 U R is the proposition that R ∈ 𝓗, U ⊆ R, and, for every R' ∈ 𝓗, U ⊆ R' implies R ⊆ R'. Thus it expresses leastness with respect to inclusion among members of the specified family containing U. This predicate by itself places no scaled-integral or other geometric condition on members of 𝓗.

HullSystem P is a type in universe max(u,v). An element H supplies a family H.Admissible ⊆ Set T such that the closure of each U ∈ H.Admissible is compact; a family H.HullRegions ⊆ Set T such that each R ∈ H.HullRegions satisfies P.IsHullRegion R; and the requirement J ∈ H.HullRegions. It also supplies a function H.hull : Set T → Set T. For every U ∈ H.Admissible, H.hull U belongs to H.HullRegions, contains U, and is contained in every R ∈ H.HullRegions containing U. Moreover, H.hull U ∈ H.Admissible. Equivalently, the supplied leastness field is P.IsLeastHullRegionIn H.HullRegions U (H.hull U), for every admissible U. The witnesses giving unit-coordinate scalings may depend on the chosen hull region.

For every such H and every U ⊆ T, the lemma subset_hull assumes hU : U ∈ H.Admissible and concludes U ⊆ H.hull U. The lemma hull_le assumes the same hU and, for any R ⊆ T, hypotheses hR : R ∈ H.HullRegions and hUR : U ⊆ R, and concludes H.hull U ⊆ R. The theorem hull_eq_self assumes both U ∈ H.Admissible and U ∈ H.HullRegions and concludes H.hull U = U. These conclusions are proved in the displayed code directly from the structure's leastness field and antisymmetry of subset inclusion. They assume the supplied structure H; they do not establish the existence of a hull system for an arbitrary P.

The function hull is defined on all subsets of T, but its leastness and admissibility requirements apply only to admissible inputs. H.Admissible may be empty; J is required to belong to H.HullRegions but not to H.Admissible. A member of H.HullRegions is not required merely by that membership to have compact closure. For an admissible input its selected hull does have compact closure, by hull_admissible and relCompact_of_admissible. No nonempty region or nonempty index type is required. If C is empty, T is a singleton and J = T; every scaled integral region is T, so P.IsHullRegion holds precisely for T, and H.HullRegions must consist of T alone. Empty specified subsets and even trivial commutative rings are permitted in general. The code contains no holomorphic functions, complex structure or holomorphic convexity condition, so the hulls here are the stated unit-scaled-set hulls; the filename does not add a holomorphic condition.

**简体中文**

设 u、v 为宇宙层级，C : Type u 为任意类型，并设 P : DirectSumPresentation.{u,v} C。对每个 c : C，P 指定交换环 A_c : Type v、A_c 上的任意拓扑，以及子集 I_c ⊆ A_c。记 T = ∏c A_c 为 P.Total，赋予积拓扑；记 J = {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ I_c} 为 P.integralRegion。对 a ∈ T，P.scaledIntegral a 是 {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • I_c}，其中 a(c) • I_c = {a(c)y | y ∈ I_c}。P.IsHullRegion R 表示：存在一个 a ∈ T，使每个 a(c) 都是 A_c 中的可逆元，且 R = P.scaledIntegral a。不要求指标类型 C 有限，不要求 I_c 为子环，也不假设乘法连续。

对任意集合族 𝓗 ⊆ Set T 和子集 U,R ⊆ T，P.IsLeastHullRegionIn 𝓗 U R 是下述命题：R ∈ 𝓗，U ⊆ R，并且对每个 R' ∈ 𝓗，若 U ⊆ R'，则 R ⊆ R'。因此，它表示 R 在指定集合族中所有包含 U 的成员里，按包含关系最小。该谓词本身没有要求 𝓗 的成员具有可逆元缩放整区域的形式，也没有施加其他几何条件。

HullSystem P 是宇宙 max(u,v) 中的类型。其元素 H 给出集合族 H.Admissible ⊆ Set T，要求其中每个 U 的闭包都紧致；给出集合族 H.HullRegions ⊆ Set T，要求其中每个 R 都满足 P.IsHullRegion R；并要求 J ∈ H.HullRegions。它还给出函数 H.hull : Set T → Set T。对每个 U ∈ H.Admissible，H.hull U 属于 H.HullRegions，包含 U，并且包含于 H.HullRegions 中每个包含 U 的区域 R。此外，H.hull U ∈ H.Admissible。等价地，所给的最小性字段要求每个容许的 U 都满足 P.IsLeastHullRegionIn H.HullRegions U (H.hull U)。用于表示可逆元逐坐标缩放的见证可以依赖于所选的包络区域。

对每个这样的 H 和每个 U ⊆ T，引理 subset_hull 以前提 hU : U ∈ H.Admissible 推出 U ⊆ H.hull U。引理 hull_le 使用同一前提 hU，并对任意 R ⊆ T，在前提 hR : R ∈ H.HullRegions 和 hUR : U ⊆ R 下推出 H.hull U ⊆ R。定理 hull_eq_self 假设 U ∈ H.Admissible 且 U ∈ H.HullRegions，推出 H.hull U = U。所示代码直接由结构中的最小性字段及集合包含关系的反对称性证明这些结论。它们都以所给结构 H 为前提，没有证明任意 P 都存在包络系统。

函数 hull 对 T 的所有子集都有定义，但最小性和输出容许性的要求只适用于容许输入。H.Admissible 可以为空；J 必须属于 H.HullRegions，但不要求属于 H.Admissible。仅仅属于 H.HullRegions 的区域不一定闭包紧致。对容许输入，由 hull_admissible 和 relCompact_of_admissible 可知，所选包络的闭包紧致。不要求区域或指标类型非空。若 C 为空，则 T 恰有一个元素且 J = T；每个缩放整区域都等于 T，因此 P.IsHullRegion 恰好只对 T 成立，而 H.HullRegions 必须只含 T。一般情形也允许指定子集为空，甚至允许交换环为零环。代码中没有全纯函数、复结构或全纯凸性条件，所以这里的包络就是上述通过可逆元缩放集合所定义的包络；文件名没有增加全纯性条件。

**日本語**

u、v を宇宙レベル、C : Type u を任意の型とし、P : DirectSumPresentation.{u,v} C とする。各 c : C に対し、P は可換環 A_c : Type v、その上の任意の位相、および部分集合 I_c ⊆ A_c を指定する。T = ∏c A_c を積位相を備えた P.Total とし、J = {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ I_c} を P.integralRegion とする。a ∈ T に対して P.scaledIntegral a は {x ∈ T | ∀c, x(c) ∈ a(c) • I_c} であり、a(c) • I_c = {a(c)y | y ∈ I_c} である。P.IsHullRegion R は、ある一つの a ∈ T が存在して、すべての a(c) が A_c の単元であり、R = P.scaledIntegral a が成り立つことを意味する。添字型 C の有限性、I_c が部分環であること、乗法の連続性は仮定されない。

任意の集合族 𝓗 ⊆ Set T と部分集合 U,R ⊆ T に対し、P.IsLeastHullRegionIn 𝓗 U R は、R ∈ 𝓗、U ⊆ R、およびすべての R' ∈ 𝓗 に対する含意 U ⊆ R' ⇒ R ⊆ R' の連言である。すなわち、指定された集合族の中で U を含むもののうち、包含関係に関して R が最小であることを表す。この述語自体は、𝓗 の要素に単元による整領域の拡縮という形や、ほかの幾何学的条件を課していない。

HullSystem P は宇宙 max(u,v) の型である。その要素 H は、各 U ∈ H.Admissible の閉包がコンパクトであるような集合族 H.Admissible ⊆ Set T、各 R ∈ H.HullRegions が P.IsHullRegion R を満たすような集合族 H.HullRegions ⊆ Set T、および条件 J ∈ H.HullRegions を与える。さらに写像 H.hull : Set T → Set T を与える。各 U ∈ H.Admissible に対し、H.hull U は H.HullRegions に属し、U を含み、U を含むすべての R ∈ H.HullRegions に含まれる。また H.hull U ∈ H.Admissible である。すなわち、最小性のフィールドは、すべての許容される U に対し P.IsLeastHullRegionIn H.HullRegions U (H.hull U) を要求する。各座標での単元による拡縮を表す証人は、選んだ包絡領域に依存してよい。

このようなすべての H と部分集合 U ⊆ T に対し、補題 subset_hull は仮定 hU : U ∈ H.Admissible から U ⊆ H.hull U を導く。補題 hull_le は同じ仮定 hU を用い、任意の R ⊆ T について hR : R ∈ H.HullRegions と hUR : U ⊆ R を仮定して H.hull U ⊆ R を導く。定理 hull_eq_self は U ∈ H.Admissible と U ∈ H.HullRegions を仮定して H.hull U = U を導く。表示されたコードは、構造の最小性フィールドと包含関係の反対称性からこれらを直接証明している。いずれも構造 H を仮定しており、任意の P に対する包絡系の存在を示してはいない。

写像 hull は T のすべての部分集合で定義されるが、最小性と出力の許容性の条件は、許容される入力だけに適用される。H.Admissible は空でもよい。J は H.HullRegions に属する必要があるが、H.Admissible に属する必要はない。H.HullRegions の要素であるだけでは、閉包のコンパクト性は要求されない。許容される入力については、hull_admissible と relCompact_of_admissible により、選ばれた包絡の閉包はコンパクトとなる。領域や添字型の非空性は要求されない。C が空なら T は一点からなり J = T である。このときすべての拡縮された整領域は T であるため、P.IsHullRegion は T に対してのみ成り立ち、H.HullRegions は T だけからなる必要がある。一般には、指定された部分集合が空であることや、可換環が零環であることも許される。コードには正則関数、複素構造、正則凸性の条件がない。したがって、ここでの包絡は上記の単元による集合の拡縮に基づく包絡であり、ファイル名から正則包という条件は加わらない。

**Paper source context (English; separate from the formal-code readback)**

**Paper source context.** Mochizuki III, Remark 3.9.5(i)–(ii) (p. 127), defines the holomorphic hull in the setting of Proposition 3.9(i) and records its fixed-point, inclusion, and monotonicity properties. Item (i) requires a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume. For relatively compact input it uses the smallest containing scaled integral region, with a nonzero multiplier in every field component. For non-relatively-compact input the paper uses the full ambient space. These qualifications remain part of the paper context.

**Implementation scope.** The five selected commands are IsLeastHullRegionIn, HullSystem, subset_hull, hull_le, and hull_eq_self. The leastness predicate is relative to any supplied class $\mathcal H$: membership in that class, containment of the input, and inclusion in every other containing member. HullSystem supplies an admissible class with compact closures, a chosen class of unit-scaled integral regions containing the integral region, a total operation, a proof of leastness on admissible inputs, and preservation of admissibility. The selected three lemmas follow from those supplied fields. There is no theorem here that such a HullSystem exists for arithmetic packets. Its admissible class may be empty, and values outside that class are unconstrained. The chosen hull class need not comprise all unit-scaled regions. In arbitrary commutative component rings, being a unit is stronger than being nonzero; no nontriviality assumption excludes zero rings. The interface’s unconstrained values outside admissibility also differ from the paper’s specified full-space branch. The file’s unselected existence-certificate constructor and closure-operator definitions are not outputs of this unit.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III: Canonical Splittings of the Log-theta-lattice* (May 2020), Remark 3.9.5(i), complete item; printed/PDF page(s) 127.

> Suppose that we are in the situation of Proposition 3.9, (i). Let
>
> $$ {}^{\alpha}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})\quad\text{(respectively, }{}^{A}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}});\quad{}^{A,\alpha}U\subseteq\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v})\text{)} $$
>
> be a subset that contains a relatively compact subset whose log-volume [cf. the discussion of Remark 3.1.1, (iii), (iv), as well as Remark 3.9.7, (ii), below] is finite [i.e., $>-\infty$]. If ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) is relatively compact, then we define the holomorphic hull of ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) to be the smallest subset of the form
>
> $$ {}^{\alpha}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}}}\quad\text{(respectively, }{}^{A}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}}};\quad{}^{A,\alpha}H\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\lambda\cdot\mathcal O_{{}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v}}\text{)} $$
>
> — where, relative to the direct sum decomposition of $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}((-))$ as a direct sum of fields [cf. the discussion of Proposition 3.9, (i)], $\lambda\in\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}((-))$ is an element such that each component of $\lambda$ [i.e., relative to this direct sum decomposition] is nonzero — that contains ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$). If ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) is not relatively compact, then we define the holomorphic hull of ${}^{\alpha}U$ (respectively, ${}^{A}U$; ${}^{A,\alpha}U$) to be $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{\alpha}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})$ (respectively, $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A}\mathcal F_{v_{\mathbb Q}})$; $\mathcal I^{\mathbb Q}({}^{A,\alpha}\mathcal F_{\underline v})$). One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined [under the conditions stated].

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III: Canonical Splittings of the Log-theta-lattice* (May 2020), Remark 3.9.5(ii), displayed properties P1–P3; printed/PDF page(s) 127.

> (P1) $\phi(H)=H$, for any $H\in\mathbb H$;
>
> (P2) $P\subseteq\phi(P)$, for any $P\in\mathbb P$;
>
> (P3) $\phi(P_1)\subseteq\phi(P_2)$, for any $P_1,P_2\in\mathbb P$ such that $P_1\subseteq P_2$.

**Actual consumer.** The graph has HullSystem→ContainerHullSystem.system→LocalEstimate→theorem110. The hull_le lemma feeds hull_subset_cont and then the local-to-global volume inequality.
